The tapetum is the innermost wall layer of the microsporangium and its cells, with dense cytoplasm and often more than one nucleus, supply nutrition to the developing…
How many microsporangia are present in a typical angiosperm anther?
Each of the two thecae has two microsporangia located at its corners, so a typical anther has four microsporangia arranged longitudinally, two in each lobe.
The proximal end of the filament of a stamen is normally attached to the
A stamen has a filament and a terminal anther; the proximal end of the filament is attached to the thalamus (receptacle) or to a petal of the flower.
The androecium of a flower, made up of stamens, is functionally the
The androecium is the male reproductive whorl of the flower, made up of stamens; the gynoecium, made up of pistils, is the female reproductive whorl.
In transverse section, a young microsporangium is bounded by wall layers totalling
In transverse section a young microsporangium is surrounded by four wall layers: epidermis, endothecium, middle layers and tapetum.
The centre of each microsporangium is occupied by a compact group of diploid cells called the
The sporogenous tissue is a compact, homogeneous group of diploid cells at the centre of the microsporangium; these cells become pollen mother cells and undergo meiosis.
The exine is the hard outer layer of the pollen wall and is made of sporopollenin, one of the most resistant organic materials known; the intine is made of cellulose…
In about 60 per cent of angiosperms, pollen grains are shed at the
In roughly 60% of angiosperms the generative cell divides into two male gametes before shedding, so the pollen grain is shed at the 3-celled stage.
For use in pollen banks, pollen grains of a large number of species are stored in
Pollen retains viability for years when stored in liquid nitrogen at –196°C; such pollen banks, like seed banks, are used in crop breeding programmes.
The intine, the inner layer of the pollen wall, is composed of
The intine is a thin and continuous inner layer of the pollen wall made of cellulose and pectin, in contrast to the sporopollenin-based exine.
The stalk by which an ovule is attached to the placenta is called the
The funicle is the stalk of the ovule; the point where the funicle joins the body of the ovule is the hilum.
Michelia is an example of a gynoecium that is
In Michelia the many pistils of the gynoecium remain free from one another, which is the apocarpous condition; in Papaver the pistils are fused, that is syncarpous.
Megasporogenesis in an ovule results in the formation of
The diploid megaspore mother cell undergoes meiosis, passing through the dyad stage, and forms a megaspore tetrad of four haploid megaspores.
The basal region of the ovule, lying opposite to the micropylar end, is the
The chalaza is the basal part of the ovule opposite the micropyle; the hilum is the ovule’s junction with the funicle.
In an ovule, the embryo sac is located within the
The nucellus, enclosed by the integuments, has abundant reserve food and encloses the embryo sac (female gametophyte); usually one ovule has a single embryo sac.
A flower whose gynoecium has more than one pistil is described as
A gynoecium with a single pistil is monocarpellary; with more than one pistil it is multicarpellary, which may be further syncarpous or apocarpous.
A mature angiosperm embryo sac is
There are 2 synergids, 1 egg, 3 antipodals and 1 central cell, making 7 cells; the central cell contains two polar nuclei, so the total number of nuclei is 8.
The filiform apparatus is a special thickening present in the
The synergids bear special cellular thickenings at their micropylar tip called the filiform apparatus, which guides the pollen tube into the synergid.
The two polar nuclei of the embryo sac are located in the
During cellularisation six nuclei are surrounded by walls; the remaining two, the polar nuclei, remain free in the large central cell.
A large feathery stigma together with light, non-sticky pollen is an adaptation for
Wind-pollinated flowers have well-exposed stamens and a large feathery stigma to trap air-borne pollen; the pollen must be light and non-sticky so that it is carried…
The PEN divides repeatedly without wall formation to give free nuclei — this is coconut water. The white kernel surrounding it is the later cellular endosperm.
Nucellar polyembryony is commonly observed in
In Citrus and mango, nucellar cells surrounding the embryo sac divide, protrude into it and develop into additional embryos alongside the zygotic embryo.
Extremely small, dust-like seeds, which aid wide dispersal, are seen in
Some seeds are extremely small and dust-like, as in orchids, Orobanche, Striga and Ficus, which helps in wide dispersal, one of the advantages seeds give angiosperms…

A seed consists of a seed coat, cotyledon(s) and an embryonal axis; the pericarp, by contrast, is the fruit wall developed from the ovary wall, not part of the seed…

The androecium of a flower is made up of
The androecium is the male reproductive whorl and consists of stamens, each stamen having a filament and an anther; the gynoecium consists of pistils.
Papaver shows which condition of the gynoecium?

The primary endosperm nucleus of an angiosperm is
It is formed by the fusion of one haploid male gamete with the two haploid polar nuclei, so it is triploid (3n).
In a grass embryo, the sheath that encloses the radicle and the root cap is the
The coleorrhiza is the undifferentiated sheath covering the radicle and root cap, whereas the coleoptile is the hollow sheath enclosing the shoot apex and leaf primordia.
Seedless bananas are produced as a result of
In parthenocarpy the ovary develops into a fruit without fertilisation, so no ovules mature into seeds. It can also be induced artificially with growth hormones.
A typical angiosperm anther is bilobed, with each lobe carrying how many microsporangia?
Each lobe (theca) of a bilobed anther carries two microsporangia at its corners, running longitudinally, giving four microsporangia in the whole anther.
A pollen grain measures roughly how many micrometres in diameter?
A pollen grain is generally spherical and measures about 25-50 micrometres in diameter, small enough to be invisible to the naked eye but visible under a microscope.
How many protective integuments typically cover an angiosperm ovule?
The ovule is covered by one or two protective integuments, which enclose it except at a small opening at the tip, the micropyle.
The mature embryo sac has how many total nuclei?

Floral rewards offered to a pollinating animal typically include nectar and
Nectar and pollen grains are the two chief floral rewards offered to a pollinator; in some plants the reward instead is a safe place to lay eggs, as in Amorphophallus.
How many nuclei are involved in triple fusion?
Triple fusion involves three nuclei: one male gamete and the two polar nuclei of the central cell, together forming the triploid primary endosperm nucleus.
The tough, protective seed coat of a mature seed develops from the

A stamen consists of a filament and a terminal
A stamen has two parts: a filament and a terminal anther; the anther is the site of pollen production, while stigma, style and ovary belong to the pistil, not the stamen.
In a typical dithecous anther, the total number of microsporangia present is
A dithecous anther has two thecae, and each theca carries two microsporangia at its corners, giving four microsporangia in total.
The inner layer of the pollen wall, made of cellulose and pectin, is the
The intine is the thin, continuous inner layer of the pollen wall, composed of cellulose and pectin, unlike the hard, sporopollenin-based exine.
In pollen grains shed at the 2-celled stage, the larger cell with abundant food reserve is the

The basal part of an ovule, lying opposite the micropylar end, is the
The chalaza is the basal part of the ovule, lying opposite the micropylar end.
The number of ovules found in the ovary of papaya or watermelon is best described as
The number of ovules in an ovary may be one, as in wheat, paddy and mango, to many, as in papaya, watermelon and orchids.
A flower whose gynoecium is made up of a single pistil is termed
A flower with a single pistil is monocarpellary; with more than one pistil it is multicarpellary, which may be syncarpous (fused) or apocarpous (free).
Cellularisation of the free-nuclear embryo sac occurs after the
After the free-nuclear divisions produce a 2-, then 4-, then 8-nucleate embryo sac, cellularisation follows, laying down cell walls around six of the eight nuclei.
The special thickenings at the micropylar tip of the synergids are collectively called the
The synergids bear special cellular thickenings at the micropylar tip called the filiform apparatus, which plays a key role in guiding the pollen tube into the synergid.
The mature embryo sac of a typical angiosperm is described as 7-celled but how many-nucleate?
Six of the eight nuclei organise into cells (2 synergids + 1 egg + 3 antipodals), while the remaining two, the polar nuclei, share one central cell, giving 7 cells…
Continued self-pollination over generations chiefly leads to
Continued self-pollination causes inbreeding depression, so many plants have evolved outbreeding devices to discourage autogamy and encourage cross-pollination.

a safe place to lay eggs

In a dicot embryo, the epicotyl ends in the

How many cotyledons does a typical dicot embryo possess?
A dicot embryo consists of an embryonal axis and two cotyledons, often fleshy with stored food, distinguishing it from the single cotyledon (scutellum) of a monocot…
The persistent, residual nucellus seen in seeds such as black pepper and beet is called
Perisperm is the residual, persistent nucellus seen in some seeds such as black pepper and beet, distinct from the endosperm, which arises after fertilisation.

Nucellar polyembryony is seen in Citrus and mango: some nucellar cells surrounding the embryo sac divide, protrude into it, and develop into additional embryos…
